text:
think it's axiomatic that pain increases ur tolerance for future pain

meaning, thick skin, so adversity seems to feel lighter

but I think what really happens, is u look back at all the good that came from bad outcomes in the past.

and u recognize that none of it could have been known ex ante.

so then the next time u get smashed by something completely senseless, tragic, and almost laughably random

you know that to search for divine design is pointless.

why?

because it has only appeared with the benefit of hindsight.

that's the benefit of experience, that's as far as you need to go in asking "why."

in these situations u are best off just shutting ur brain down. 

otherwise u go down a rabbithole of all the good you've done recently, and u feel some divine injustice, as if a good outcome was promised to you.

this causes u to question all ur beliefs, the idea that life is fair when it feels so unfair to you, and you're just in a state of agita which no man has ever been able to permanently settle.

so instead of doing all that, u block and tackle and go with what u know has worked.

u shrug and u say,

"I'll figure it out," because u always have.

u say,

"I don't know what good will come of this, but something will," because it always has.

and as an ex-military friend is quite fond of saying,

"shit makes great fertilizer."

trust in the divine presence, and know that u will only see it in the rearview.
 
off u go kiddo 🫡
